svg.title: Collapse of the Eastern Bloc (1989–90) and Dissolution of the USSR into 15 Independent States (December 1991)
svg.desc: Pearson Edexcel GCSE History chronological atlas map showing the 1989 revolutions across Poland (June 1989 Solidarity), Hungary (May–September 1989 open Austrian border), East Germany (9 November 1989 Berlin Wall and 3 October 1990 Reunification), Czechoslovakia (November 1989 Velvet Revolution), Bulgaria, and Romania (December 1989), alongside the independence of the Baltic Republics (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania) and the December 1991 breakup of the USSR into 15 independent states.

g.text: • Berlin Wall falls after Leipzig protests
AUGUST COUP & END OF THE USSR (AUG–DEC 1991)
• 19–21 Aug 1991: Yeltsin defeats hardline 'Gang of Eight' coup.
• 8 & 21 Dec 1991: Belavezha Accords & CIS replace USSR.
• 25 Dec 1991: Gorbachev resigns; USSR splits into 15 states.
3 Baltic + 3 Slavic + Moldova + 3 Caucasus + 5 Central Asian
EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · OPTION P4: COLLAPSE OF THE SOVIET UNION
Collapse of the Eastern Bloc (1989–90) & End of the USSR (Dec 1991)
EDEXCEL EXAM TAKEAWAY · FROM THE 'SINATRA DOCTRINE' TO SUPERPOWER COLLAPSE
Abandoning the Brezhnev Doctrine triggered Eastern Europe's 1989 domino revolutions, German reunification
(Oct 1990), Warsaw Pact dissolution (July 1991), and—after the failed August 1991 coup—the breakup of the USSR.
